blocks.text: The main point: there are no freehold condos in Sardis South. The two condo buildings, Skynest (Watson Road) and The Yearling (Chilliwack River Road), are both on leased First Nations land, and the other apartments are purpose-built rentals or manufactured-home parks.
Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: "Sardis South" is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack; the City publishes no boundary for it.
Plans: Sardis South is in the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan area of the 2050 Official Community Plan, which also includes the Agricultural Area Plan and the development permit areas.

Where the apartments are: two leasehold buildings, Skynest at Watson Road and Vedder Road (45745 and 45757 Watson Road) and The Yearling in the Iron Horse community (6045 Chilliwack River Road), plus a purpose-built rental building on Vedder Road (McGill Apartments).

Sardis South's "condo market" is a leasehold market. Both of its modern apartment buildings stand on Tzeachten First Nations land (Skynest at Watson/Vedder, The Yearling at Iron Horse) — the buildings are new (2022–2024), the amenities are real, and the tenure is leasehold in both cases, so every freehold assumption (Form B, depreciation report, PTT/GST treatment, lender terms) has to be re-derived from the lease documents.

The Yearling is marketed two ways. The developer sells its 86 condos to buyers, while a rental site markets units in the same building to tenants and notes that the Residential Tenancy Act doesn't apply on Tzeachten land. If you're buying as an investor, look into the tenancy rules as well as the sales material.

A 45+ label here isn't a strata bylaw. Skynest's and Promontory Lake Estates' 45+ rules are in lease and park documents, where BC's strata rule (only 55+ is allowed) doesn't apply. The only strata age rule here is at the Higginson Villas townhouses, listed as 55+.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Sardis South

items.t: Skynest, 45745 and 45757 Watson Road (Phases 2 and 1): condos on leased Tzeachten First Nation land, marketed by the developer as 45+. There's no Form B for these units; the lease and community rules are the documents to check.

The Yearling (Iron Horse), 6045 Chilliwack River Road: a six-storey building of 86 condos, built in 2024 by Diverse Properties, on leased Tzeachten First Nation land in the Iron Horse community. It's leasehold, not freehold.
The Grove — 44523 McLaren Drive. Townhouse. Freehold strata, built 2007 — the strongest Sardis candidate. Documented, not counted
Higginson Villas, 45752 Stevenson Road: townhouses. Sources disagree about it, so confirm the ownership type and any age rule on its Form B.
Wealick Place — 6029 Promontory Road. Townhouse-form (Row / Townhouse).

Both modern apartment buildings stand on Tzeachten First Nations land (Skynest 2022/2023 phases on Watson Road, The Yearling 2024 on Chilliwack River Road) — every freehold assumption (Form B, depreciation report, PTT/GST treatment, lender terms) has to be re-derived from the lease documents for the specific unit.

A 45+ label here isn't a strata bylaw. Skynest's 45+ rule is in its lease documents, outside the strata rule that only 55+ age bylaws are valid. The only strata age rule here is Higginson Villas' 55+; confirm it on the Form B, not the listing.

Sardis South has no City-published boundary; it is the southern part of Sardis in the City of Chilliwack, around Tyson Road, South Sumas Road and Watson Road, roughly south of Stevenson Road.
The whole of Sardis, including Sardis South, sits inside Schedule B5 (Sardis) of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500.
Sardis South is a Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board area name, and that board publishes statistics only for its whole area.
Vedder Road is the eastern edge: Sardis East Vedder and Promontory lie east of it, Sardis West Vedder west of it, and Vedder Crossing and Garrison Crossing lie to the south toward the Vedder River.

blocks.text: Sardis South: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) allows 3 to 4 units on eligible single-detached and duplex zoned lots over 280 square metres inside the urban growth boundary, under Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395.
New secondary suites are not permitted below the flood construction level, which limits basement suites on the Vedder River side of Sardis South.
Short-term rentals are a regulated use under Short-Term Rental Bylaw 2021, No. 5141, not an as-of-right use of a house.

blocks.text: Sardis South: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Route 58 Tyson is the Sardis South bus: a loop from Cottonwood Mall via Tyson Road at Keith Wilson Road and Tyson Road at Watson Road, running roughly hourly on weekdays.
Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road, is a Fraser Valley Regional Library branch, not a City library.
Sardis Sports Complex is at 5725 Tyson Road, on the City's facility list, a short walk from Mount Slesse Middle School at 5871 Tyson Road.
SD33 is consulting on balancing enrolment because the district is at 103 percent of functional capacity, so Sardis-area catchment boundaries may change for September 2027.
The Vedder River dike and the river's alluvial fan sit south of the neighbourhood; flood construction levels are lot-specific, not street-specific.

blocks.text: Sardis South: development and new projects

items.t: Sardis Secondary expansion, 45460 Stevenson Road: a $40-million expansion adding 400 student seats, bringing capacity to 1,600, with a gymnasium refurbishment. Status: reported as a School District No. 33 capital project on the project tracker (as of November 3, 2026).
BC Transit runs Chilliwack transit, not TransLink; Route 58 Tyson loops through Sardis South from Cottonwood Mall via Tyson Road.
Route 51 Vedder runs the Vedder Road corridor at the east edge of Sardis South, between the University of the Fraser Valley Chilliwack campus and Downtown Chilliwack.
Route 54 Promontory crosses the Stevenson Road side via Wiltshire Street at Stevenson Road and Promontory Road at Vedder Road.
Route 66 Fraser Valley Express, the regional link to Lougheed Town Centre Station, stops at Vedder Road at Luckakuck Way, north of Sardis South.

blocks.text: Sardis South: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the lot against the City's floodplain maps under Floodplain Regulation Bylaw No. 4519 before subjects: the bylaw sets a 75-metre setback from the Vedder River's natural boundary and flood construction levels vary by area.
Lots near creeks fall under Development Permit Area 3, which protects riparian areas and fish habitat; a development permit can be required before building.
